newsitem.title: TURKEY: New Turkey government says no ethnic Kurd problem.
newsitem.headline: New Turkey government says no ethnic Kurd problem.

text.p: Turkey's new government says in its coalition protocol distributed on Monday that a Kurdish rebel campaign in the southeast of the country is caused not by ethnic sentiment but by poverty and foreign provocation.

"The problems of southeast Anatolia do not spring from ethnic causes, but from geographical, social and economic causes, from the region's feudal structure, foreign plans and provocations," the document says.
Conservative Mesut Yilmaz was appointed prime minister on Monday to replace Islamist Necmettin Erbakan who resigned two weeks ago.
The government vowed to strongly oppose Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas, fighting for Kurdish self rule since 1984.
Previous governments and the influential army have refused to negotiate with the PKK, which they regard as a terrorist group.

"The struggle against separatist terror will be continued effectively and will be given full guarantee under the rules of the constitutional state," says the protocol, a contract between Yilmaz and his two coalition partners outlining future government policy.
More than 26,000 people have been killed in the conflict between Turkish troops and the PKK in Turkey and northern Iraq.
Security forces killed six guerrillas in recent fighting in the southeast province of Hakkari, Anatolian news agency said.
It did not say when the clashes took place and no military casualties were reported.
